rule: Elixir: ... `def unquote(:name)` with a literal name is `Mod.name`
notes: call_type convention (SPEC gives no Elixir mapping; Elixir has no methods and the `macro` type is defined only for C/C++/ObjC and Rust `name!`): every local, imported and remote call is direct, a call through a value is callback. Operators and special forms (`|>`, `=`, `case`, `fn`, `%{}`, `__MODULE__`) are language constructs, not calls. `def unquote(:hello)(name)` defines `MyApp.Named.hello`; `unquote` in the function head is part of the declaration, not a call. Calls in its body have that caller; the local call `hello(n)` resolves to it, high.
